messages:
Alex K: Quick signal: sampling + compacting still losing billing metadata (~0.3% of envelopes). Seen on per-tenant rollups.
Priya R: Ugh. We tried fp/backfill last quarter. What's the failure mode now?
Alex K: Reorder + late-drop of the span that carried the header. compactEnvelope() ends up with empty root.meta in those edge cases.
Diego M: Two rough paths: 1) move metadata promotion earlier (edge), 2) make a low-latency side-channel that always carries minimal attribution (a tiny beacon).
Liam S: Beacon? Like an independent, unsampled fire-and-forget message per request with billing_key/fingerprint? That adds QPS but is tiny.
Priya R: How is that different from pre-enrich? If edge already writes root, why need beacon?
Diego M: Beacon is separate because it bypasses sampling/reorder: edge emits main sampled trace + a tiny beacon proto to a dedicated ingest topic that we guarantee delivery for (at-most-once acceptable). The main envelope stays sampled; beacon carries only attrs used for billing/quota.
Alex K: Pros: avoids increasing envelope size for sampled payloads, preserves correctness for attribution. Cons: extra topic + small QPS and eventual consistency if beacon lost.
Liam S: Also need to consider ordering: beacon may arrive after compacted envelope. But we can upsert billing_key when beacon arrives; that means ingestion needs idempotent update logic keyed by request_id or trace_id.
Priya R: Latency: for quota enforcement we need sync availability at edge. Beacon can't help route-layer quota checks. So we still need edge resolution for quota-enabled routes. Beacon covers attribution only.
Diego M: Implementation sketch: - Edge computes minimal meta: {req_id, billing_fp, ts} and publishes to topic beacon-meta-v1. - Beacon consumer upserts into small hot store (per-day partition) keyed by req_id -> billing_fp. - Ingest compact job, when seeing empty billing_key, checks hot store for req_id and fills before indexing. - Metric: `ingest.beacon_hits` / `ingest.beacon_misses`.
Liam S: Cost calc: extra 1k QPS * 40 bytes = ~3.4GB/day. If we keep beacons only for routes with known missing issues (configurable), overhead is tiny. Hot store can be Redis or Dynamo with TTL 1h.
Priya R: Privacy/regulatory: ensure beacon payload excludes PII, only hashed fingerprint + tenant-id token. Use salt rotation and HMAC.
Alex K: Nice. Action items: Priya prototype beacon emitter in edge with config `edge.beacon.routes = ["/v1/generate"]`; Diego wire up consumer that writes to redis TTL 1h; Liam produce cost delta + failure-mode numbers. Canary 72h.
ingest-bot: beacon-ingest.alpha | beacon-queue-len=12 | beacon_hits=0.998 | beacon_misses=0.002
Diego M: I'll spin up a canary producer on /v1/embed for 48h first. Priya I'll pair with you on the edge flag.
Liam S: I'll model redis cost and index upsert load; preliminary says negligible for targeted routes.
Priya R: Also adding a `billing.confidence` tag: `beacon_resolved|edge_resolved|missing` so analytics can filter.
Alex K: Good. If canary reduces missing from 0.3% -> <0.05% we consider rollout. If not, fallback to forcing pre-enrich on high-QPS routes.
Diego M: Opening INF-8230 for the canary. Will link PRs here.
Alex K: Thanks :thumbsup:
